supporting_observations.claim: The alerted HTTPS activity is recorded as proxy CONNECT traffic to update.routewise.com, matching the RouteWise update service identified in the inventory as approved and checking about every five minutes.
The proxy connections recur at roughly five-minute intervals from 13:41 through 14:10 UTC.
The 13:41 RouteWise connection is associated with routewiseupd.exe (PID 3828); later connections are also attributed to that same process connecting through the proxy.

The recorded RouteWise connection pattern and process attribution support a benign updater-check explanation for the alerted activity; the available records do not show a different process or destination driving that pattern.

known_telemetry_limitations: The RouteWise records show proxy CONNECT metadata and connection summaries, not the HTTPS request or response contents.
The available records show RouteWise connections beginning at 13:41 UTC; they do not establish whether the alert-reported activity occurred from 13:30 to 13:41.
The proxy records identify the hostname, but the evidence provided does not establish the external destination IP, certificate details, or integrity of the updater binary.
claims_not_established: The records do not establish what content, if any, was exchanged inside the RouteWise TLS sessions.
The records do not establish whether routewiseupd.exe or its installation was independently verified as authentic beyond its recorded path and process identity.
unrelated_findings: Separate review: Chrome accessed customer.cloud.com/Citrix/StoreWeb, a service not listed among approved software and services in the supplied inventory; this is outside the alerted RouteWise activity. (T126-00160, T126-00161, T126-00169, T126-00170, T126-00172)

Separate review: WS-DREYES-01 authenticated as kim.nguyen to WS-KNGUYEN-01 using NTLM around 13:47 UTC. The environment context says remote administration is only performed from WS-PBECKER-01; the records do not establish the purpose of this authentication. (T126-00213, T126-00214)

Separate review: WS-KNGUYEN-01 made an SMB connection to FILE-COP-01 that generated an ANONYMOUS LOGON event. The records do not identify what was accessed. (T126-00291, T126-00292, T126-00293, T126-00295)
Separate review: kim.nguyen ran PowerShell with ExecutionPolicy Bypass to execute C:\Scripts\backup-check.ps1. This is not shown to be related to the RouteWise connections. (T126-00189, T126-00190)
